svg.title: The Compton effect
svg.desc: A photon of energy E = hf and wavelength λ strikes an electron e− at rest and scatters off at a right angle as a photon of lower energy E′ = hf′ and longer wavelength λ′. The electron recoils with kinetic energy KE_e = E − E′, carrying the momentum the photon lost. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Compton scattering conserves energy and vector momentum
Momentum vectors form a closed triangle
A 100 keV photon scatters from an initially resting electron. E = E′ + K e; electron rest energy is
retained in the recoil relation. Vector lengths represent momentum.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
